items.stem: Complete the statement: Activity-based costing assigns overheads to products …
options: in proportion to direct labour hours only
according to the activities they consume
items.answer: according to the activities they consume
items.markingKey: ABC: cost pools → driver rates → products by driver usage [1].

items.stem: Complete the statement: Interest cover is calculated as …
options: interest payable ÷ profit for the year
items.answer: profit from operations ÷ interest payable
items.markingKey: Interest cover = PBIT / finance costs [1].

items.stem: During a review at Galaxy Ltd it was found that any user can change the bank details of suppliers. Explain the risk this creates and recommend a control.
items.answer: Allows payment fraud; restrict to authorised users and require independent verification.
items.markingKey: Risk identified [1]; consequence explained [1]; appropriate control [1] [3]

items.stem: Galaxy Ltd spent $133,000 on research into a water filtration unit and $103,000 on development after all IAS 38 criteria were met. Calculate the amount charged as an expense and the amount capitalised.
items.answer: Expense $133,000; capitalised $103,000
items.markingKey: Research $133,000 expensed [1]; capitalise $103,000 [1]

items.stem: Ibis plc needs funds for a new factory in Kenya. It issues $400,000 7% debentures 9 months before its year end. Profit from operations is $335,000 and equity is $760,000. (a) Calculate the debenture interest charge for the current year and for a full year. (b) Calculate the interest cover for the current year and for the next full year (assuming profit is unchanged). (c) Calculate the gearing ratio after the issue (debentures / (equity + debentures)).
Complete the statement: Staff resistance to a new computerised system is best reduced by …
options: consulting staff and providing training before implementation
items.answer: consulting staff and providing training before implementation
items.markingKey: Change management: consultation and training [1].

items.stem: Complete the statement: A master budget consists of …
options: the budgeted income statement, budgeted statement of financial position and cash budget
items.answer: the budgeted income statement, budgeted statement of financial position and cash budget
items.markingKey: Master budget summarises functional budgets [1].

items.stem: In the draft statement of cash flows of Sirocco plc, the increase in inventories of $22,500 was added in reconciling profit from operations to cash generated from operations. Explain the error and calculate its effect on the reported cash generated from operations.
items.answer: The increase in inventories should be deducted. Cash generated from operations is misstated by 2 × $22,500 = $45,000 (overstated).
items.markingKey: Correct treatment (deducted) [1]; reason linked to cash [1]; effect $45,000 overstated [1] [3]

items.stem: Priya and Ines share profits 1:1. On a change in the profit-sharing ratio the following revaluations were agreed — Premises: increased by $72,200; Equipment: reduced by $9,400; Inventory: written down by $3,200. Calculate the profit or loss on revaluation and each partner's share.
items.answer: Revaluation profit $59,600: Priya $29,800, Ines $29,800
items.markingKey: Gains: Premises $72,200 ; losses: Equipment $9,400, Inventory $3,200 [1 per 2 items]; net profit $59,600 [1]; shared 1:1 old ratio [1]

items.stem: At 30 April 2026 the equity of Monarch plc was: ordinary shares of $1 $700,000, $90,000 redeemable preference shares of $1, share premium $81,000, retained earnings $891,000. During the following year: (1) a 1 for 5 rights issue was made at $1.20 and fully taken up; (2) all the preference shares were redeemed at a 5% premium out of retained earnings; (3) $350,000 5% debentures were issued on the first day of the year. (a) Calculate the debenture interest for the year and state where it appears in the financial statements. (b) Prepare the equity section of the statement of financial position after these transactions (ignore the profit for the year).
items.answer: (a) $17,500; finance costs in the income statement (b) Ordinary shares $840,000; share premium $109,000; CRR $90,000; retained earnings $796,500; total $1,835,500
items.markingKey: (a) $350,000 × 5% [1]; finance cost [1] [2] (b) Each correct line [1 each, max 4]; total $1,835,500 [1] [5]

items.stem: Complete the statement: When shares are redeemed entirely out of distributable profits, the amount transferred to the capital redemption reserve equals …
options: the proceeds of a new share issue
the nominal value of the shares redeemed
items.answer: the nominal value of the shares redeemed
items.markingKey: CRR = nominal value redeemed − proceeds of any new issue [1].

items.stem: Complete the statement: In the consignee's books, the consignor appears as …
options: a personal account (the consignor is a creditor for sales proceeds less expenses and commission)
items.answer: a personal account (the consignor is a creditor for sales proceeds less expenses and commission)
items.markingKey: Consignee records sales, expenses and commission in consignor's account [1].

items.stem: The sales manager of Delta Ltd changed the selling price from $45 to $42.00. The sales price variance was $19,590.00 A and the sales volume variance $8,977.50 A. Explain how the two variances may be linked and whether the decision was successful.
items.answer: A price cut is likely to raise volume. Net effect $28,567.50 A, so the decision reduced profit compared with budget (other factors such as market conditions may also explain volume).
items.markingKey: Price elasticity link [1]; net effect calculated [1]; judgement with caveat [1] [3]

items.stem: Vanguard Ltd is evaluating a delivery van fleet costing $155,000 with a life of 4 years and no residual value. Depreciation is straight-line. Net cash inflows: year 1 $45,500, year 2 $39,000, year 3 $42,000, year 4 $57,500. Calculate the accounting rate of return based on the initial investment.
items.markingKey: Total profit = $184,000 − depreciation $155,000 = $29,000 [1]; average profit $7,250 [1]; initial investment $155,000 [1]; ARR = 4.7% [1]

items.stem: The draft profit of Osprey Ltd for the year is $244,000 and closing inventory is $169,000. The auditors find: (1) inventory includes goods at cost $22,500 with NRV of $20,000; (2) purchases of $9,000 for the current year were omitted from the records in error; (3) the directors have revised the useful life of machinery, so the depreciation charge for this year should be $8,000 instead of the $18,000 included. (a) Calculate the revised profit for the year. (b) State and explain how IAS 8 classifies item (3).
items.answer: (a) $242,500 (b) Change in accounting estimate: applied prospectively from the current year, no restatement of prior years.
items.markingKey: (a) $244,000 − $2,500 (NRV) − $9,000 (purchases) + $10,000 (depreciation) = $242,500 [4] (b) Classification [1]; prospective treatment [1] [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: The most appropriate cost driver for quality inspection costs is … (b) Complete the statement: The most appropriate cost driver for purchasing department costs is …
items.answer: (a) the number of inspections (b) the number of purchase orders placed
items.markingKey: (a) Inspection cost driven by inspections [1]. (b) Ordering costs vary with number of orders [1].

items.stem: Complete the statement: A merger differs from a takeover because …
options: it is not allowed for sole traders
one business is always bought for cash
the combining businesses agree to join on broadly equal terms to form one entity
items.answer: the combining businesses agree to join on broadly equal terms to form one entity
items.markingKey: Merger: agreed combination; takeover: one acquires control of another [1].

items.stem: In a joint venture with Samuel, Nadia paid expenses of $21,200 and Samuel received all the sales of $36,900. Nadia recorded both the expenses and Samuel's sales in his own joint venture account and treated the balance as profit. Explain the error.
items.answer: Nadia's joint venture account should record only Nadia's own transactions (expenses $21,200) and his share of profit; Samuel's sales belong in the memorandum JV account, which is used to calculate profit.
items.markingKey: Own transactions only [1]; profit from memorandum account [1]; balance represents amount due, not profit [1] [3]

items.stem: A project has an NPV of $9,507 at 10% and -$4,281 at 20%. Estimate the internal rate of return by interpolation and state whether the project is acceptable with a cost of capital of 12%.
items.answer: IRR ≈ 16.9%; acceptable

items.stem: Monarch plc has a draft profit of $783,000. The directors have capitalised: research costs $60,000, development costs meeting all IAS 38 criteria $324,000, a patent bought during the year for $107,000 (legal life 5 years, full year's amortisation), and an internally generated brand valued by the marketing director at $490,000 (credited to profit). (a) Calculate the intangible assets to be shown in the statement of financial position. (b) Discuss the ethical issues raised by the directors' treatment.
items.answer: (a) $409,600 (b) Overstating profit and assets misleads shareholders and lenders; may be motivated by bonuses; breaches integrity/objectivity; auditors should insist on correction.
items.markingKey: (a) Development $324,000 + patent $107,000 − $21,400 = $409,600 [3] (b) Two issues [2]; consequence [1] [3]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: A master budget consists of … (b) Complete the statement: Zero-based budgeting means …
items.answer: (a) the budgeted income statement, budgeted statement of financial position and cash budget (b) each budget is built from zero and every item must be justified
items.markingKey: (a) Master budget summarises functional budgets [1]. (b) ZBB: no automatic base from last year [1].

items.stem: Complete the statement: Discounting cash flows takes account of …
items.answer: the time value of money
items.markingKey: $1 today is worth more than $1 in future [1].

items.stem: Jonas's business (valued at $280,000) and Lina's business (valued at $210,000) merged. The adviser proposed issuing 245,000 shares of $1 to each owner. Explain why this may be unfair and calculate a fair allocation.
items.answer: Shares should reflect the value each owner contributes: Jonas 280,000 shares, Lina 210,000 shares. Equal allocation transfers value from the owner of the larger business.
items.markingKey: Unequal contributions [1]; Jonas 280,000 [1]; Lina 210,000 [1] [3]

items.stem: Extracts for Osprey Ltd for the year ended 31 December 2026: revenue $1,150,000, cost of sales $632,500, expenses $356,000, opening inventory $199,000, closing inventory $169,000, trade receivables $265,000, cash $32,000, trade payables (the only current liability) $35,000, capital employed $1,223,000. Calculate the profit margin (profit from operations ÷ revenue), liquid (acid test) ratio.
items.answer: profit margin 14.0%; liquid 8.49:1

items.stem: Isla and Hana, sharing profits 3:1, dissolve their partnership. Their statement of financial position shows: non-current assets $139,000 (including a car at $11,000), inventory $11,200, trade receivables $17,800, bank $6,000, trade payables $17,300, capital Isla $88,700, capital Hana $68,000. Other non-current assets were sold for $161,100, inventory for $7,000 and receivables realised $16,900. Isla took the car at $8,500. Payables accepted $16,700 in full settlement and dissolution costs were $3,300. (a) Calculate the amount paid to each partner to close the business. (b) Prepare the bank account to show that it closes with a nil balance.
items.answer: (a) Isla $97,300, Hana $73,700 (b) Funds available $171,000 = payments to partners $171,000

items.stem: Which is a cost of computerisation that a small business often underestimates?
options: Staff training and disruption during changeover
items.answer: Staff training and disruption during changeover
items.markingKey: Hidden costs: training, data conversion, lost productivity [1].

items.stem: Complete the statement: Under IFRS 3, purchased goodwill is …
options: tested for impairment annually and not amortised
items.answer: tested for impairment annually and not amortised
items.markingKey: Goodwill: annual impairment review [1].

items.stem: Osprey Ltd made a 1 for 10 bonus issue on 140,000 ordinary shares of $1. The bookkeeper debited the bank account and credited share capital with $14,000. Explain the error and state the correct entry.
items.answer: No cash is received in a bonus issue. The correct entry is Dr share premium (or other reserves) $14,000, Cr ordinary share capital $14,000.
items.markingKey: Bonus issue raises no cash [1]; Dr reserve $14,000 [1]; Cr share capital $14,000 [1] [3]

items.stem: Monarch plc budgets sales of 10,100 units in July, 5,100 units in August. Closing inventory of finished goods each month is to be 20% of the following month's sales. Inventory at the start of July is 1,400 units. Prepare the production budget for July.
items.answer: July 9,720 units

items.stem: Banyan Ltd has a draft profit of $526,000, current assets $259,000 and current liabilities $125,000 at its year end. After the year end: a customer owing $27,000 at the year end went into liquidation; a flood destroyed inventory bought after the year end costing $43,000. At the year end a former employee was claiming $34,000 for unfair dismissal; lawyers think the claim will probably succeed. (a) Calculate the current ratio before and after the adjustments. (b) Discuss whether the directors should be allowed to omit the provision because "the case has not been decided yet".
items.answer: (a) 2.07:1 → 1.46:1 (b) No: a present obligation from a past event exists, outflow is probable and estimable, so IAS 37 requires a provision; omitting it overstates profit and misleads users.
items.markingKey: (a) $259,000/$125,000 [1]; ($232,000)/($159,000) [2] [3] (b) IAS 37 criteria applied [2]; consequence for users/ethics [1] [3]
